articles.title: Tigers' Comerica Park Renamed Ahead of 2027 MLB Season, Details Revealed
articles.summary: The Detroit Tigers will not be playing in Comerica Park next season.
articles.body:
The Detroit Tigers will not be playing in Comerica Park next season.

No, they aren't changing stadiums. But their home digs will be renamed to Fifth Third Park next season, per Jason Beck of MLB.com, after Fifth Third Bank acquired Comerica Bank last October.

Detroit's naming-rights deal with Comerica Bank—which began in 2000—lasts through 2034.

"We believe we have a responsibility to be good stewards" of Detroit's ballpark, Fifth Third Bank officials said in a press conference on Monday.

articles.title: Cubs 3B Alex Bregman reportedly sustains multiple fractures from being struck in the face by foul ball
articles.summary: Bregman left Sunday's win over the Reds after an errant ball off the bat of teammate Michael Busch hit him on the left cheekbone.
articles.body:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman has reportedly sustained multiple facial fractures from taking a foul ball to the face on Sunday, per ESPN's Jeff Passan . Bregman was hit in the left cheek while in the on-deck circle during Sunday's win over the Cincinnati Reds . He quickly left the game while holding a towel to his face.

Bregman will not need surgery for the injuries, per Passan, and is expected to return in time for the playoffs. The Cubs are currently one game from clinching a postseason berth .

Bregman appeared to be in relatively good spirits after the injury, posting multiple photos of his very swollen and bruised face on Instagram — first on Sunday after the game and another on Monday morning.

"Thanks for all the messages y'all," Bregman wrote in Sunday's post. "I'll be back."

The scary incident occurred in the fourth inning of Sunday's game, with Cubs first baseman Michael Busch up to bat and Bregman warming up in the on-deck circle. A pitch clipped Busch's bat and hit Bregman in the face.

The collision, and its immediate aftermath, wasn't initially visible on the broadcast. An alternate angle of the moment shows the ball hitting Bregman in the left side of the face, near his eye.

Bregman dropped his bat and his helmet and jogged along the side of the dugout, clutching his face in obvious pain. Chicago staff came over to give the infielder a towel, which Bregman held to his face as he doubled over.

Bregman's face was clearly bleeding as he headed to the locker room, with the infielder appearing to have sustained a laceration on his left cheek, near his left eye.

Busch quickly dropped his bat and squatted to the ground after the accidental contact, then finished the at-bat, hitting a single. Bregman was replaced by Matt Shaw as a pinch hitter.

As the inning ended and the Cubs went back on defense, Shaw stepped in at second base, with Pedro Ramirez moving over to fill Bregman's role at third.

After the game, Cubs manager Craig Counsell told reporters that Bregman was in the hospital receiving more tests. He confirmed that the ball had hit Bregman's left cheekbone.

Counsell said Bregman's face was "pretty swollen," but he didn't have more updates on the infielder's condition.

Prior to exiting, Bregman hit an RBI single to put the Cubs on the board in the first inning and drew a walk in the third inning, with the third baseman later scoring. Chicago went on to beat the Reds 9-1 .

The Cubs are back in Chicago, preparing for the team's final home series of the regular season against the Miami Marlins , which begins Tuesday.

articles.title: Trumpeter Dr Jesse McGuire belts national anthem after instrument malfunctions in unforgettable MLB moment
articles.summary: The Arizona Diamondbacks' 2001 World Series anniversary featured a trumpet malfunction that turned into an unforgettable national anthem moment.

McGuire was known to perform the national anthem during that postseason, which included a decisive World Series Game 7 walk-off victory over the New York Yankees, whom the Diamondbacks just so happened to schedule their 25-year World Series anniversary for during their weekend series. McGuire tried to correct it, but after realizing in the beginning of The Star-Spangled Banner that it wouldn’t cut it, he reacted in the best way possible. McGuire sang the rest of the way. articles.title: MLB awards check-in: Front-runners for MVP, Cy Young, Rookie of the Year and Reliever of the Year
articles.summary: With one week left in the regular season, "Baseball Bar-B-Cast" took one last look at the races for baseball's major awards.
articles.body:
With one week left in the 2026 MLB regular season, the awards races are nearing their conclusion. On the latest episode of "Baseball Bar-B-Cast," hosts Jake Mintz and Jordan Shusterman ran through the baseball awards one more time and highlighted the front-runners for each.

Let's dig in, going from the most decided awards to the most wide-open awards with just a few games left to play.

Front-runner: Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong

This award has seemingly gone from Shohei Ohtani 's to lose to a tight race between Ohtani and Crow-Armstrong to PCA leaving no doubt in the final months of the season.

"It was like, 'This is going to be one heck of a debate. This is going to be an amazing race. Can PCA's defense outrank Ohtani's pitching?' It was going to be really interesting," Shusterman said. "Instead, PCA has run away with the lead in WAR to a degree that frankly I don't remember seeing."

PCA has hit 45 home runs, a Cubs record for a left-handed hitter, and he leads baseball with 10.4 fWAR, which is nearly 4 WAR ahead of Ohtani in second at 6.8.

"Yes, Ohtani tailed off in terms of his production and then his availability," Mintz said, "but it's not as if PCA just played out the string. He earned it, and he took it with his play and his production in a way that really no one saw coming."

Front-runner: Padres closer Mason Miller

"With all due respect to Mason Montgomery and Jhoan Duran and Adrian Morejon, this is Mason Miller, and it won't be that close," Mintz said, noting that he thinks Miller will win unanimously.

Miller's strikeout rate is particularly remarkable. As Shusterman noted, we've gotten used to seeing strikeout rates around 35% from relievers. But Miller's strikeout rate is 48% this season.

Front-runner: Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski

For a while, this was shaping up to be a race between Misiorowski and the Phillies ' Cristopher Sánchez. Sánchez still leads Misiorowski in innings, but the Brewers ace's other numbers stand alone. Among those: a 38.2% strikeout rate and 6% walk rate.

Misiorowski currently holds the record for lowest batting average against for a qualified starting pitcher in baseball history. "We'll see if that holds all the way until the end of the season, but that would be another feather in his cap in just a ridiculous season that has maybe made him the best pitcher in the world," Shusterman said.

Front-runner: Yankees ace Cam Schlittler

A few weeks ago, this seemed like a contest between Schlittler and the Blue Jays' Dylan Cease , but Schlittler has put some distance between himself and the field in recent weeks.

"Schlittler is not slowing down, whatsoever," Shusterman said. "And once we start previewing October, we're going to be like, 'Yeah, have fun beating this guy.'"

The Rays ' Drew Rasmussen and the Guardians' Parker Messick are the other names in contention for this award, but at this point, it's a race for second.

This is the first year that Reliever of the Year is among the BBWAA awards, so as the hosts noted, we don't know what voters will prioritize or value most.

But Mintz thinks Baker will win. "He has more saves than baseball teams do," he said, noting that Toronto 's Louis Varland , Cleveland 's Cade Smith and Boston 's Aroldis Chapman should also receive votes.

Front-runners: Astros DH Yordan Alvarez and Rays 3B Junior Caminero

The last three awards are still up in the air, and AL MVP is a two-horse race. Junior Caminero has made a strong push with the AL-best Rays in the second half. Meanwhile, Yordan Alvarez has been dominant all season and has been doing his part to try to lead the Astros back to the postseason.

"I think that Yordan being a primary DH is going to be something that more voters care about than you expect ," Mintz said. "… And that's not to say that Caminero is a Gold Glover at third base, no. The most amazing thing about his season is that he will start every single game at third base."

Caminero will be the first player in the American League to do so since Cal Ripken. Also, he has hit 41 home runs with an .892 OPS and helped the Rays to the best record in the American League.

But with his 1.027 OPS, Shusterman contended, Alvarez has been the best hitter in the American League the entire season. In a down year for Aaron Judge and Shohei Ohtani, Alvarez, while he doesn't play defense, has separated himself from the rest of the sport in terms of offensive production.

Front-runner: Tigers INF Kevin McGonigle and Guardians SP Parker Messick

For both rookie awards, voters have to debate the value of a pitcher vs. the value of a hitter, which makes for a difficult decision between the top two candidates.

"Is it Kevin McGonigle, who's going to play nearly every game in the Tigers' infield? He has a .376 on-base, he's 21 years old, more walks than strikeouts — it's an incredible season," Shusterman said. "Or, do you take a Parker Messick, who only gets so many opportunities to make an impact, but he's been unbelievable? One of the best pitchers in the American League, one of the lowest ERAs to start a career in baseball history."

Front-runner: Mets SP Nolan McLean and Reds 1B Sal Stewart

In the NL, it's a similar debate between a pitcher in McLean and a hitter in Stewart, with a nod to Cardinals second baseman JJ Wetherholt and his elite defense.

But Stewart, Mintz noted, is on pace to play all 162 games , which will make him only the fourth rookie to ever accomplish that feat.

"When it comes to Rookie of the Year, give me homers, give me RBI," Mintz said. "Did the guy bang? I'll take that over the defense any day."

articles.title: All 30 MLB Teams' Worst Player of 2026 Regular Season
articles.summary: For some players, the 2026 MLB season can't end soon enough.
articles.body:
For some players, the 2026 MLB season can't end soon enough.

For just about 180 days' worth of games, most of us have been delighted by the ascendant stars such as Pete Crow-Armstrong, Jacob Misiorowski and Cam Schlittler. Yet all 30 fanbases also know the horrors of the other side of the spectrum, where the worst players in the league reside.

We're going to dispense with courtesy and point an accusing finger at every team's worst player of the 2026 season. This is mostly about production, but also about which players really hurt a given team. The bigger the waste, the larger the crime.

We'll go division by division, starting in the AL East and ending in the National League West.

By WAR, there are definitely worse players on the 2026 Orioles. That means you, Dylan Beavers. It also means you, Trey Gibson, Dean Kremer and Andrew Kittredge.

At a certain point, though, it's the sheer size and emptiness of a sample size that stands out. Taveras has gotten 474 plate appearances this year. He has only rewarded the Orioles with a 78 OPS+. Only nine players are in that particular club, as six of them have more rWAR than Taveras.

Lest anyone forget, Narváez was Boston's catcher on Opening Day this year. He was meant to be their No. 1 behind the plate, and deservedly so after a 2025 season that resembled a breakout.

Instead, he was so bad on both sides of the ball (including a 52 OPS+ in 197 plate appearances) that the Red Sox felt compelled to do a Hail Mary trade for Adley Rutschman in August. That has yet to yield short-term returns. The long-term risk of it blowing up in Boston's face is very real .

Doval was an All-Star closer for the Giants in 2023. There was some hope that he could revert to that form when the Yankees acquired him at the deadline in 2025.

He instead posted a 4.54 ERA in 44 appearances this year, after which the Yankees gave up and shipped him to Pittsburgh. It was a case of addition by subtraction for their bullpen, though uncertainty remains about whether the team has a setup man as good as Doval was supposed to be .

The Rays have their share of less-than-awesome players, but they've been pretty good at limiting exposure to the truly bad ones. But with Matz, they haven't had much choice but to keep using him.

He's on a two-year, $15 million contract, which is on the steep side by Rays standards. Yet even though they've tried everything to get him into a groove, his ERA is over 5.00 as a starter and a reliever over 77.0 total innings.

When the Blue Jays re-signed Scherzer earlier this year, they likely didn't expect him to live up to his Hall of Fame future. They just needed him to anchor the back end of what looked like a strong rotation.

Instead, he's had the worst year of his career, making only 16 starts and posting a 6.07 ERA. Because of injuries, the pain of this performance has only been magnified in a Toronto rotation that has never really had momentum.

Chicago White Sox: INF/OF Luisangel Acuña

To be fair, Edgar Quero has taken exactly as many plate appearances (217) as Acuña and has been even more of a straggler, to the tune of -0.8 rWAR. At least he's off the roster, whereas Acuña is still doing the bad kind of damage.

He has only a 47 OPS+ for the season, making him 53 percent worse than the average hitter. Among hitters with at least 200 plate appearances, only three have been less productive at the plate.

Because of a back injury, Hoskins hasn't suited up for the Guardians since August 18. Maybe it's not a coincidence that they're 20-10 since then?

It's a mean thing to say about a genuinely likeable player who has had a really good major league career. But then again, when you're a bat-only player who can only hit .179 with a 93 OPS+, you have to know there's no avoiding shade.

As bad as Jahmai Jones was (i.e., 24 OPS+) as a Tiger, at least they only gave him 105 plate appearances before moving on. By comparison, Vierling got 291 turns at the plate before a groin injury ended his season in late July.

With these, he somehow regressed even further from last year's 75 OPS+ to a 64 OPS+ this year. Even if using him as an everyday center fielder wasn't necessarily the plan, here's hoping the Tigers have learned their lesson.

What a career Perez has had. He's been an All-Star nine times and a World Series champion once. He can claim to have held the catcher home run record for a time before Cal Raleigh came along.

We bring all this up to help soften the blow of what has been by far the worst season of Perez's 15 years in the big leagues. Even if he can still handle himself behind the plate, nobody likes looking at a .227/.271/.374 slash line. That's over 604 plate appearances.

Minnesota Twins: RHP Simeon Woods Richardson

Woods Richardson made only 12 appearances as a Twin, ultimately covering just 47.2 innings. As far as sample size goes, this should put him more in misdemeanor territory than felony territory.

You see those numbers. Now dig these: He had a 7.74 ERA with 26 strikeouts and 25 walks, as the Twins went 2-10 in his 12 appearances.

It's a thankless job pitching for the A's. Yet someone has to do it. Nobody knows that better than Springs. He's made a team-high 28 starts.

In these starts, he has a 6.18 ERA. You probably don't need me to confirm it, but here goes anyway: That is by far the highest ERA of any starter who has made at least 28 starts this season.

There's always intrigue whenever the Astros acquire a new pitcher. Perhaps it's a bit dusty at this point, but they have a history of finding guys who had been missing something and then helping them find it.

They couldn't do so with Burrows, who's only now on a rehab assignment since injuries forced him out of the rotation in early July. He had a 5.99 ERA in 18 appearances earlier in the year, 11 of which resulted in Houston losses. With the Astros fighting for their lives in the AL West, that sure looks relevant now.

Los Angeles Angels: RHP Grayson Rodriguez

For our purposes, the Angels represented a target-rich environment. Do you have any idea how bad Christian Moore, Logan O'Hoppe and Moisés Ballesteros were/have been for them? Look it up.

Even so, Rodriguez's 5.96 ERA over 93.2 innings hurts the Angels a little more. Remember that they gave up Taylor Ward to get him. He still has 1.8 rWAR, even after a late-season slide with Seattle.

Refsnyder only took 129 plate appearances for the Mariners. It did cross our mind that maybe that's too few to throw a tantrum over.

Then again, he did this after signing for $6.25 million, and he really was that bad. The 35 OPS+ was bad. Given his job description as a platoon right-handed hitter, the .506 OPS against lefties was even worse.

Smith was the Rangers' Opening Day second baseman and seemingly set to be a solid regular there all year. He had been a Silver Slugger in 2024. He still salvaged a 100 OPS+ even after regressing in 2025.

Well, he's in Toronto now precisely because his 69 OPS+ over 154 plate appearances basically broke Texas' plan at second base. Ezequiel Duran's rise is a related story, but it matters that the Rangers went 18-27 in the 45 games Smith played.

Playoff Predictions Entering Last Week 🔮

As bad as his WAR is, the real number that stands out with Kim is his -3 OPS+. You don't often see a negative OPS+, much less from an actual hitter rather than a pitcher.

How many hitters in the live-ball era have taken at least 130 plate appearances and posted a negative OPS+? Just three: Andy Anderson in 1949, Cam Callagher in 2023 and Kim in 2026.

The Marlins went unusually out of their way to sign Fairbanks last winter, inking him to a one-year, $13 million contract after their cross-state rivals in St. Petersburg cut him loose. For this, they thought they were getting a closer.

Instead, they got arguably the most volatile reliever of the 2026 season. Fairbanks struck out 57 batters in 41.1 innings but also allowed eight home runs and 32 runs overall. He was apparently battling thoracic outlet syndrome, necessitating season-ending surgery .

We can have an honest debate about whether Kodai Senga belongs here, but at least he's redeemed himself a bit since he moved to the bullpen. There will be no such redemption for Polanco, whose season ended in August because of ankle surgery .

Even sans context, a .148/.201/.230 slash line over 145 plate appearances is pretty dismal. And lest anyone forget, the context in this case concerns how Polanco was meant to be Pete Alonso's replacement. Mets fans don't seem convinced .

Speaking of palace intrigue, the Phillies' one-year, $10 million deal with García was meant to help them forget about Nick Castellanos before he was even off the roster. They planned to slot García into right field, a spot normally reserved for Castellanos.

Not that Castellanos did any better (he was actually worse) following his eventual release, but to call García a bust would be underselling it. He got 259 plate appearances before season-ending surgery in June. He only managed a 60 OPS+ with an inflated 32.4 K%.

Here's one you don't see very often: In 116.0 innings pitched across 25 total appearances for the Nationals, Mikolas gave up more home runs (27) than walks (23).

You know, just in case anyone was still wondering where his 5.82 ERA came from. The Nationals finally gave up and released Mikolas in August, potentially spelling the end of the 38-year-old's career.

Cabrera should be a really fun pitcher. He averages 96.5 mph on the fastball. His changeup can and will go higher than that. It's been clocked at 97.1 mph, which should be the ultimate reminder that modern pitchers have gone too far.

In reality, he's had an up-and-down career that hit a low point this year. At least he's healthy, but a 5.67 ERA and 1.450 WHIP are not what the Cubs had in mind when they traded their No. 1 prospect for Cabrera in January.

Even before 2026, Hayes dared to answer a question nobody was asking: How bad does a guy have to be at the plate before even his Gold Glove defense is no excuse to keep playing him?

Well, now we're really finding out in 2026. Hayes has gone from a 63 OPS+ across 2024 and 2025 to a mere 20 OPS+ this season. The best thing he's done all year is make John Sadak blow his stack . That's only because of the unavoidable yucks.

This time last year, Frelick was putting the finishing touches on what looked like a breakout season. He finished with an 111 OPS+, which paired nicely with his Gold Glove-caliber defense in right field.

Well, now his OPS+ is down to a career-low 72. He's barely breaking even defensively, with a -2 DRS and +1 OAA. A shoulder injury didn't help his throwing, but no such convenient excuse can completely wash away the broader disappointment of his season.

Ozuna came back from the brink by slamming 79 home runs for the Braves across the 2023 and 2024 seasons. Even though he regressed in 2025, the Pirates made a $12 million bet on the possibility that he still had some of that juice left.

He did not. Before being released in August, Ozuna managed only a 66 OPS+ and eight home runs in 280 plate appearances. As the 35-year-old has yet to catch on with a team since then, his career may actually be over this time.

St. Louis Cardinals: LHP Matthew Liberatore

Only 32 pitchers have made at least 30 starts in 2026. Liberatore is one of them. That, plus 149.2 innings pitched, gives him a certain amount of value that is hard to measure in an era where starters just don't work as much.

Even so, this is another Jeffrey Springs conundrum. Durability is nice, but Liberatore has done more harm than good when he's pitched. His ERA is 5.36. He's served up 27 home runs, so it's no wonder the Cardinals have lost 16 of his 30 starts.

The lizard-brained among us still see Gallen's name and have a little "Ace!" lightbulb go off in our heads. At least, that's how it works for yours truly, who still remembers when Gallen was a Cy Young Award contender.

In actuality, he's a guy with a 6.12 ERA over 104.1 innings. That -1.6 rWAR would be the worst among all pitchers with at least 100 innings this year… if not for this next guy.

It isn't actually that rare for a pitcher to allow over 100 earned runs in a season. What is rare is doing it in fewer than 130 innings. With 127.1 innings and 102 earned runs, Lorenzen is only the sixth pitcher to ever do it.

To be fair, he threw 11.2 innings and allowed 11 runs when he joined the Blue Jays. But when you're a pitcher that even the Rockies are comfortable releasing, well, that's just never a good sign.

So far, we've done our best to avoid dunking on guys who have been really bad in small sample sizes. Díaz arguably deserves the same measure of grace, as he's made only 18 appearances and logged 15.2 innings this year.

And yet, it seems appropriate to make him an exception to the rule. He's the only $23 million-per-year reliever in MLB. The Dodgers surely expected more than 26 hits, 11 walks and 18 earned runs allowed in his 15.2 innings. Their only hope now is that injuries are to blame for all that has gone wrong.

For a team that's on track to make the playoffs, the Padres are a surprisingly target-rich environment for bad players. Yes, we did consider Nick Castellanos and Casey Mize for this spot.

Canning gets the boot instead because of the depth of the damage he's caused. He's fourth on the team with 83.2 innings pitched, so there's real pain reflected in his 5.59 ERA. Most notably, the Padres are 2-9 in his 11 starts.

The Giants didn't have a set closer back on Opening Day, but Walker pretty much had first dibs on the gig. Even if he'd had a rough one in 2025, he was a genuine relief ace with a 1.91 ERA over 80.0 innings the year before.

This didn't pan out. Walker's form has indeed only gotten uglier, resulting in a 7.16 ERA and 1.806 WHIP over 32.2 innings. He has barely more strikeouts (23) than walks (19).

Stats courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .

articles.title: Everything at Stake in MLB's Final Week of 2026 Season
articles.summary: There's no going back now. The 2026 MLB season has reached its final week, and it can't be emphasized strongly enough how much is up in the air.
articles.body:
There's no going back now. The 2026 MLB season has reached its final week, and it can't be emphasized strongly enough how much is up in the air.

Six playoff spots are still up for grabs, including three tied to American League division titles. We also have a Triple Crown pursuit, a home run race going down to the wire, and all sorts of odds and ends that might surprise you.

Come, let us take a deep breath and dive deep into all that these last six days will determine.

Playoff Predictions Entering Last Week 🔮

Note: All odds are according to FanDuel .

All 3 American League Division Races are Undecided

Tampa Bay Rays: 95-60 -- GB (4 at NYY, 3 at PHI)

New York Yankees: 89-66, 6.0 GB (4 vs. TBR, 3 vs. BAL)

This one is pretty much wrapped up, as the Rays have a magic number of just 2 heading into a seven-game road trip that starts with a double-header against the Yankees on Tuesday. The Rays should be able to finish this one off.

Cleveland Guardians: 81-75 -- GB (3 at BOS, 3 at KCR)

Chicago White Sox: 80-76, 1.0 GB (3 at KCR, 3 vs. COL)

Everyone else in the AL Central has been eliminated, so it's just the Guardians and White Sox duking it out for the division title and (as of now) the AL's No. 2 seed and a first-round bye.

The White Sox have the softer landing, whereras the Guardians have momentum. They're 12-7 in September, with the White Sox hitting the skids at 8-11. That sure looks like it's going to end up being the difference in this race.

If it comes down to a tie, the White Sox would win courtesy of a 7-6 head-to-head record against the Guardians.

Odds to Win AL Central: Guardians -124, White Sox +106

Texas Rangers: 78-78 -- GB (3 vs. NYM, 3 at MIN)

Houston Astros: 77-79, 1.0 GB (2 at SEA, 4 at ATH)

Seattle Mariners: 73-83, 5.0 GB (2 vs. HOU, 4 vs. LAA)

Yes, the Mariners are improbably still alive in the AL West. Their "tragic number" stands at 2, so they basically need to win out and hope the Rangers and Astros do nothing but lose.

The Rangers have the edge because they have gone 10-8 in September, compared to 7-11 for Houston. Yordan Alvarez has tried to rally the troops , but Astros fans should be warned: Seattle has had Houston's number in recent seasons, and the A's have been playing spoiler lately.

The Astros went 9-4 against the Rangers, so they would have the advantage in the event of a tie.

Odds to win AL West: Rangers -146, Astros +126

There Are Still 4 Wild Card Spots Available

* New York Yankees: 89-66, +9.5 GB (4 vs. TBR, 3 vs. BAL)

* Boston Red Sox: 84-72, +4.0 GB (3 vs. CLE, 3 vs. CHC)

Chicago White Sox: 80-76, -- GB (3 at KCR, 3 vs. COL)

Toronto Blue Jays: 77-80, 3.5 GB (2 at BAL, 3 vs. CIN)

Houston Astros: 77-79, 3.0 GB (2 at SEA, 4 at ATH)

Baltimore Orioles: 76-81, 4.5 GB (2 vs. TOR, 3 at NYY)

One takeaway here is how much is at stake in the AL West race between the Rangers, Astros and Mariners. It's already win-or-go-home for the Mariners, while neither the Rangers nor the Astros can count on the wild card as a safety net.

The AL Central contenders have more wiggle room, though both the Guardians and White Sox need to mind their tiebreakers . The Guardians only hold a tiebreaker over the Orioles, while the White Sox have tiebreakers on Toronto and Texas in addition to Cleveland.

The Red Sox can't catch the Rays, but they could still hypothetically steal the No. 4 seed from the Yankees. That would set up a Wild Card Series between the two clubs at Fenway Park instead of Yankee Stadium.

Chicago Cubs: 87-69, +1.0 GB (3 vs. MIA, 3 vs. BOS)

San Diego Padres: 87-69, +1.0 GB (3 at LAD, 3 vs. ARI)

Philadelphia Phillies: 86-70, -- GB (3 vs. MIL, 3 vs. TBR)

Arizona Diamondbacks: 82-74, 4.0 GB (3 at COL, 3 vs. SDP)

Nobody here has clinched a playoff spot, though there's no doubt that the Cubs have the strongest hand. They hold tiebreakers over all three pursuers: San Diego, Philadelphia, and Arizona.

The Phillies hold the tiebreaker over the Padres, but not the Cubs. As such, they'll need to claim the top spot and No. 4 seed outright if they want to host a Wild Card Series at Citizens Bank Park.

The D-backs didn't help their cause with losses in five out six between September 12 and 18, but they did rally to win the last two of a three-game set against the Yankees. Their upcoming series against San Diego could prove crucial, as it will decide the two team's tiebreaker.

Pete Crow-Armstrong Goes for the HR Title and a 40-40 Season

It's still technically possible for Caminero, Olson or Alvarez to claim MLB's overall home run title, but even calling it "unlikely" feels like a kindness. This race is between PCA and Schwarbs.

Schwarber already has a pair of NL home run titles, but he's not the hotter slugger of the two as we head into the home stretch. Crow-Armstrong has seven home runs in September, compared to Schwarber's five.

Meanwhile, PCA also needs just two stolen bases to notch the seventh 40-40 season in major league history. After stealing two bases in his last 10 games, he needs to pick up the pace.

Yordan Alvarez Goes for the AL Triple Crown

It's close between Alvarez and Simpson, but the former has been heating up since his batting average dropped to .310 for a couple of days earlier in September. He went 8-for-20 in Houston's last two series, while Simpson is "only" hitting .301 in September.

Just to make sure they get credit, don't count out Ben Rice (39) or Pete Alonso (39) coming from behind in this race. Yet all eyes are on Caminero and Alvarez, who have homered four times and three times in September, respectively.

This is where Alvarez really needs to get on his horse, as he's already let Alonso take over the RBI lead this month. Alonso has driven in 17 runs in September, compared to Alvarez's five.

Luis Arraez Goes for a 4th Batting Title, with a Twist

Arraez is batting .313, giving him a comfy six-point cushion over Gabriel Moreno (.307) for the NL lead. If he holds on, he would win his fourth batting title… with his fourth different team. That would be a first for MLB history .

Jacob Misioroski and Cam Schlittler Chase MLB History

Misiorowski has a 1.86 ERA and 247 strikeouts, while Schlittler has a 1.94 ERA and 234 strikeouts. If they keep their ERAs under 2.00, this will be the first season since 1972 with two pitchers with a sub-2.00 ERA and 230-plus strikeouts.

The Astros threw a combined no-hitter on May 25, but there still hasn't been a no-no by a single pitcher since Blake Snell in 2024. If the drought continues, 2025 and 2026 would become the first back-to-back seasons without a no-hitter by a single pitcher since 1932-1933.

While fellow future Hall of Famer Max Scherzer's 2027 plans remain unclear, Verlander said 2026 will be his last MLB season. The three-time Cy Young Award winner is tentatively set to take the mound one last time for the Detroit Tigers on Saturday against the Pittsburgh Pirates.

Elly De La Cruz needs two home runs and two stolen bases to secure his first 30-30 season.

Chandler Simpson is four stolen bases away from 50.

Alec Burleson (111) leads Sal Stewart (110) by one in the NL RBI chase.

Michael Wacha needs 5.2 innings in his last start to reach 200 for the season.

Bryan Baker (40) has a one-save lead on Cade Smith (39) in the AL.

Riley O'Brien (38) has a one-save lead on Mason Miller (37) in the NL.

Aaron Nola and Shota Imanaga (34) are trying to avoid leading MLB in home runs allowed.

The Milwaukee Brewers need two more wins for their first 100-win season.

The Colorado Rockies' next loss will make it 100 for a fourth year in a row.

Stats courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .

articles.title: Red Sox should want to face Yankees’ Aaron Judge in postseason
articles.summary: Aaron Judge isn’t the same Aaron Judge
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox are going to face the New York Yankees in the American League Wild Card Series.

It's still unclear whether or not they'll face Aaron Judge …

Judge, who has been dealing with several different injuries this season, suffered a calf strain last week and was placed on the injured list (retroactive to Thursday) on Saturday. Judge is obviously going to be frustrated with situation, but perhaps even more so after he spent the majority of the regular season sidelined with a fractured rib and will likely finish the campaign slashing .241/.360/.511 with 18 home runs and 41 RBIs in 66 games — not exactly what we all expected.

"I'd like to be back by the postseason," Judge told MLB Media's Bryan Hoch . "That's definitely the plan. [It's the] 10-day IL, so the 10th day is probably the last game of the season. We'll see. I've got really no answers for you on any timeline or anything like that."

It's pretty difficult arguing that you want to face the reigning AL MVP and one of the two best hitters of the 2020s, but let's all be serious about the reality of the situation. If he makes his way back into the lineup for the postseason, you'll be pitching to someone who has been sidelined for the majority of the last four months. It's not like he's been the same guy since returning earlier this month, either, as he went just 4-for-23 (.174) with one home run across six games since being activated on Sept. 8.

Judge at 50% is still better than most at 100%, but it is important to remember that he has found it somewhat difficult to stay productive in past postseasons.

Aaron Judge – Postseason 2025 : 13-for-26 (.500 BA) 2024 : 9-for-49 (.184 BA) 2022 : 5-for-36 (.139 BA) 2021 : 1-for-4 (.250 BA) 2020 : 4-for-30 (.133 BA) 2019 : 9-for-34 (.265 BA) 2018 : 8-for-19 (.421 BA) 2017 : 9-for-38 (.188 BA)

2-for-8 in terms of productive stretches. 58-for-246 in terms of at-bats. 0-for-forever in terms of making enough of an impact to actually be considered a winning baseball player.

The Yankees absolutely would prefer to have him in the lineup, but it's not an obvious choice right now. If they have to force him in they'll either lose Luis Garcia Jr. or Ben Rice as the designated hitter or put someone with a bum calf in the outfield at Yankee Stadium. If they choose to let him fully heal and miss that first series, they can play both Rice (.889 OPS) and Garcia (.843 OPS) while having the space to play guys like Spencer Jones (1.177 OPS vs. LHP), and Paul Goldschmidt (.997 OPS vs. LHP).

I know which scenario I would rather see.

articles.title: Former Mets Backstop Suddenly Ends Career Just 8 Days Before Season Finale
articles.summary: The New York Mets received a sudden retirement announcement from a 14-year professional catcher who saw a brief stint with the team.
articles.body:
The New York Mets ' 2026 season is nearing its conclusion after a year that fell well short of expectations surrounding the club entering the campaign.

New York was mathematically eliminated from playoff contention earlier this month, leaving the Mets with only a handful of games remaining before their season finale on September 27.

"A 7-2 loss to the Phillies (on Sunday) was a fitting end to the home slate of a season that went off the rails in April and never recovered," Tim Britton wrote for The Athletic . "The Mets' 36-45 record in Queens this season is their worst since 2012. It was the first time they finished below .500 in a full season at home since 2018."

But just eight days before the Mets officially close out their season with a road game against the Washington Nationals , a former New York catcher announced that his own baseball career is over.

Former New York Mets Catcher Makes Retirement Decision Shortly Before End Of Season

Chance Sisco , who Mets fans will remember as a member of the 2021 team, revealed that he is retiring from professional baseball after more than a decade.

"After 14 years of playing professional baseball, I've decided it's time to retire from playing the game I've dedicated most of my life to," Sisco wrote on Instagram . "Baseball has given me more than I could have ever imagined. The opportunity to play for organizations like the ( Baltimore ) Orioles , Mets, ( Seattle ) Mariners , ( Minnesota ) Twins, ( St. Louis ) Cardinals , (Long Island) Duck's and ( Chicago ) Dog's, compete at the highest levels, and make memories that will stay with me forever is something I'll always be grateful for."

Sisco entered professional baseball as a second-round pick of the Orioles in the 2013 MLB Draft and quickly established himself as one of the organization's more promising catching prospects. He won the South Atlantic League batting title in 2014 after hitting .340 and later represented Baltimore in the 2016 All-Star Futures Game.

He reached the major leagues with the Orioles in 2017 and spent parts of five seasons with Baltimore before the Mets claimed him off waivers in June 2021. Sisco appeared in only five games for New York, recording one hit and one RBI before being designated for assignment that September.

Across 517 at-bats with Baltimore and New York, Sisco hit .197 with a .317 on-base percentage and .334 slugging percentage. He finished with 16 home runs.

Former New York Mets Catcher Ends Long Baseball Journey

Sisco continued searching for opportunities after leaving New York, spending time with the Mariners and Twins organizations before moving into independent baseball.

His career eventually took him to the Ducks, where he found another productive chapter. He also played for the Dogs and produced a .301 batting average with 17 home runs and 61 RBIs in 2025.

Now, with the 2026 MLB season approaching its official end, Sisco has decided his playing days are over. His career included stops across affiliated and independent baseball, with the Mets representing only a brief chapter — but one that remains part of the 14-year journey he reflected on while announcing his retirement.
